content:
The first 20 minutes of the match were played with considerable intensity, until after the 'water break', both sides had players shown yellow cards – England's midfielder Elliot Anderson and Argentina's central defender Lisandro Martínez. Up until half-time, almost every time the whistle blew, fans would cheer for their own team and boo the opposition's fouls.

The two sides were level at half-time, but after switching ends in the second half, in the 55th minute England's Anthony Gordon received the ball and broke the deadlock to give England a 1-0 lead, prompting celebrations from England fans throughout the venue.

After falling behind, Argentina fought back immediately, launching three attacks down the right flank with crosses into the box within 10 minutes, but all were blocked, drawing sighs from many Argentina supporters. It was not until the 85th minute that Enzo Fernández headed in a pass from Messi to level the score at 1-1, sending Argentina fans into delirium with drumming and vuvuzelas blaring.

In stoppage time in the 92nd minute, Messi provided the assist for Lautaro Martínez to score the decisive goal against England, sending Argentina through to the final to face Spain for the World Cup trophy. Argentina fans once again erupted in wild celebrations, and even after the final whistle blew, they continued embracing and celebrating, with some holding up cardboard cutouts of Messi from the mall.

Argentina fan Ah Ho said he had been a Messi supporter since the latter made his debut at Barcelona. Wearing the 'two-star' Argentina No. 10 jersey, he said this World Cup would be Messi's last, as he attempts to defend the title. While his idol Messi and the team have sparked controversy during the tournament, Ah Ho believes that rather than getting bogged down over refereeing decisions in every match, fans should cherish Messi's final days representing his country. He also joked that 'while I'm still young enough to handle it,' he chose to stay up late and watch at the mall with other fans, saying the atmosphere was even better than watching at home. In the end, the result went his way as Argentina advanced to the final.

England fans chanted 'Football's coming home!' throughout the tournament but failed to bring the trophy back once again. Declan, who is studying in the UK, returned to Hong Kong during the summer break. Today, draped in the England flag, he cheered passionately with his friends during the fierce battle between the two sides. He said this was his first time watching a match at a mall to soak up the atmosphere, and felt that while the fans were passionate, they respected each other and there were no overly heated confrontations.

Despite the heartbreak of defeat, Declan – who shares a name with England midfielder Declan Rice – believed England had performed well in the match. Having supported the team for two tournaments, he said frankly: 'We've waited 60 years – waiting another four years is no big deal!'

Argentina will face Spain on the 20th in a bid to retain the title, while in the third-place playoff England will take on France on the 19th.
